derivations.claim: Construct the normalized Gaussian comparison law, prove every moment and compute its characteristic function by real integration by parts.
Use the explicit 2n-th sine difference identity, local CF equality, Fatou, then dominated convergence to force exact Gaussian even moments without prior moments.
Obtain all moments by differentiation and all exponential absolute moments by monotone convergence of cosh, then globally identify the CF by dominated Taylor series.
Prove equality of the Gaussian-smoothed densities by a derived Gaussian Fourier identity and an absolutely convergent Fubini interchange.
Recover all bounded continuous test integrals, then all half-lines using deterministic continuous ramps and conclude equality of Borel laws.

derivations.claim: Construct C2 local continuous logarithms from the finite second moments and nonvanishing near zero.
Factor the joint CF in both independent coordinate systems, remove the discrete logarithmic ambiguity on a ball, and differentiate mixed Hessian entries.
Vary one independent source coordinate on the orthogonal ball to force a shared source logarithm to be exactly quadratic near zero; apply the proved Gaussian extension lemma.
Apply the contrapositive and unit column norm to characterize every nonGaussian column as a signed coordinate vector.

Let $S=(S_1,\ldots,S_p)^T$ have mutually independent centered real coordinates with $\mathbb E S_i^2=1$, and let $O\in\mathbb R^{p\times p}$ be orthogonal. Suppose the coordinates of $T=OS$ are mutually independent. If column $i$ of $O$ contains nonzero entries in two different rows, then $S_i$ has the standard Gaussian law. Thus each non-Gaussian source column has exactly one nonzero entry, which is $1$ or $-1$.

Use the shared-column lemma and column orthogonality to prove a signed permutation, including the possible oneGaussian source and p=1 boundary.
Set Q=O transpose and obtain the exact two asserted matrix and law identities.
